# Command line

<!-- BEGIN GENERATED: cli -->
Everything the `git terrace` command line accepts, read from the same definition
the binary parses with. `git terrace --help` and `git terrace <command> --help`
print the same text. The global flags work on every command.

## `git terrace`

Browse a git repository in your browser, offline.

```sh
git terrace [OPTIONS] [PATHS]... [COMMAND]
```

- `--ref <A..B>`: Open the compare page for `A..B` (commits in B that A lacks)
  or `A...B` (since B left A, from their merge base) in the first repository,
  starting a server if needed. An empty side is `HEAD`. Combine with `--print`
  to print the URL.
- `--print`: With `--ref`: print the URL instead of opening a browser.

## Global flags

- `<PATHS>...`: Repositories to serve (any path inside one), or folders to
  search two levels deep. Other commands use the first. Default: `.`.
- `--addr <ADDR>`: Address to listen on. Local only by default. Overrides
  `server.addr`.
- `--no-watch`: Do not watch for changes: no live updates, and a restart or
  reload picks up new commits. Overrides `watch.enabled`.
- `--config <DIR>`: Folder holding `config.toml` (and `actions.toml`). Default:
  the XDG config folder.
- `--no-actions`: Never run user actions, even when `actions.toml` declares
  some.
- `--public`: Serve read-only to other machines: committed history only.
  Required with any `--addr` that is not loopback. Overrides `server.is_public`.

## `git terrace serve`

Serve the repository in the browser (the default).

```sh
git terrace serve [OPTIONS] [PATHS]...
```

## `git terrace config`

Print the effective configuration and where each value comes from.

```sh
git terrace config [OPTIONS] [PATHS]...
```

## `git terrace mcp`

Run a read-only MCP server over stdio for agents.

Reads the repositories the paths name (folders are searched as for `serve`).
With `--served` it also reads every repository served before, such as those of a
running server. Tools then take a `repo` name from `list_repos`.

```sh
git terrace mcp [OPTIONS] [PATHS]...
```

- `--served`: Also read the repositories served before (the registry a running
  server keeps).

## `git terrace insights`

Print one insight of the first repository as JSON, or list them: the numbers of
the web pages, `/api/v1/insights/{name}` and the MCP `insight` tool, byte for
byte. Reads the repository of the current folder, offline.

```sh
git terrace insights [OPTIONS] [NAME] [PATHS]...
```

- `<NAME>`: The insight to compute. Omit it to list every insight.
- `--rev <REV>`: Branch, tag, sha or HEAD. Default HEAD.
- `--period <PERIOD>`: `1w`, `1m`, `3m`, `1y` or `all` (default).
- `--q <Q>`: Commit filter, as the web pages' text, e.g. `author:ann !merge`.
- `--label <LABEL>`: `kind` (default) or `scope`, for the label insights.
- `--metric <METRIC>`: `commits` (default), `added`, `deleted` or `net`, for
  `contributors`.
- `--limit <LIMIT>`: Most rows, for the insights that list rows.
- `--path <PATH>`: Focus file, for `coupling`.
- `--support <MIN_SUPPORT>`: Shared commits a pair needs, for `coupling`.
  Default 3.
- `--cross-dir <CROSS_DIR>`: `1` lists pairs across directories too, for
  `coupling`.
- `--author <AUTHOR>`: The person to report, for `knowledge_risk`. `--path`
  drills a directory.
- `--json`: List as JSON too. An insight is always printed as JSON.

## `git terrace open`

Open a `gitterrace://` or `/go` permalink in the browser, starting a server if
needed.

The clone is found among repositories served before and under `links.roots`. An
unknown repository exits 2, with no clone and no network.

```sh
git terrace open [OPTIONS] <LINK> [PATHS]...
```

- `<LINK>`: `gitterrace://<id>/<sha>[/<path>][#L<a>-L<b>]`, an
  `http(s)://.../go/...` URL or a bare `/go/...` path.
- `--print`: Print the URL instead of opening a browser.

## `git terrace launch`

Open the running server in the browser as its owner, so actions and settings can
write.

Pages are readable by any user of this machine over loopback, so writes need
proof only you hold: this reads the secret in your 0600 state file and opens a
one-time link that sets a session cookie. `--print` prints the link instead (it
works once, for a minute).

```sh
git terrace launch [OPTIONS] [PATHS]...
```

- `--print`: Print the link instead of opening a browser.

## `git terrace remove`

Take a repository off the running server. Its pages then answer 404.

The opposite of serving a repository while a server already runs: the server on
`server.addr` is found and checked the same way. The on-disk index stays, so
serving it again is fast. The last repository stays served.

```sh
git terrace remove [OPTIONS] [TARGET] [PATHS]...
```

- `<TARGET>`: A path inside the repository, or its URL name. Default: the
  current repository.

## `git terrace install-handler`

Register (or with `--uninstall` remove) this program as the `gitterrace://` link
handler.

Opt-in. macOS writes `~/Applications/gitterrace-open.app`, Linux a `.desktop`
file, and WSL and Windows only print the steps. It prints exactly what it wrote.

```sh
git terrace install-handler [OPTIONS] [PATHS]...
```

- `--uninstall`: Remove what a previous install wrote.

## `git terrace service`

Run the server at login: print, install or uninstall a systemd user unit or
launchd agent.

The unit runs this program with the given paths (made absolute) and `--addr` if
set, restarts on failure and logs to journald (Linux) or
`~/Library/Logs/gitterrace.log` (macOS). It never sets `--public`. `uninstall`
removes only a file this command wrote. Windows is not supported.

```sh
git terrace service [OPTIONS] <ACTION> [PATHS]...
```

- `<ACTION>`: `print` the unit, `install` it, or `uninstall` it. One of `print`,
  `install`, `uninstall`.
- `--now`: With `install` or `uninstall`: also run the enable/start (or stop)
  command.

## `git terrace init`

Write a documented `config.toml` and the pre-filled `actions.toml` to the config
folder.

`config.toml` is a template with every setting commented out at its default.
`actions.toml` has the Send to targets and example actions. Those that need your
own settings start switched off. An existing file is kept as it is. To start
over, move the file away and run this again.

```sh
git terrace init [OPTIONS] [PATHS]...
```

## `git terrace export`

Write a static copy of the site to a folder, for sharing or hosting.

```sh
git terrace export [OPTIONS] [OUT] [PATHS]...
```

- `<OUT>`: Folder to write into (created if missing). Default:
  `./gitterrace-export`. Give it first, before any repositories:
  `export site repo1 repo2`. A folder an earlier export made is replaced whole.
  Any other non-empty folder is refused without `--force`, and so are a symlink
  and a folder holding a repository being exported. An export folder that
  records no ownership is refused: remove it and export again.
- `--force`: Write into a non-empty folder that no earlier export made. Its
  files are kept, a file in the site's way is replaced, a folder in its way
  fails the export. Later exports replace only what an export put there.
- `--commits <N>`: Newest commits to include as pages. Default: `500`.
- `--file-kb <KIB>`: Largest file to include as a page, in KiB. Larger files are
  left out of the export. Default: `512`.
- `--export-pages <N>`: Most pages to write, folded diff fragments included.
  Overrides `limits.export_pages`. Unset, every page in scope is written. Past a
  set cap the export stops and writes nothing.
- `-q`, `--quiet`: Print no progress. Progress goes to stderr: one updating line
  on a terminal, a line every few seconds otherwise.
- `--project <NAME=URL>`: Credit a repository that is someone else's project (a
  demo), as `name=url`: its pages name and link it in the snapshot banner.
  `name` is the repository's folder name. Repeat it for several repositories.
